sections.subtitle: Noun Gender: Masculine & Feminine
sections.content:
⚖️ All Nouns Have Gender

General Rules:
• -o endings → masculine
  → el libro (book)
  → el gato (cat)
• -a endings → feminine
  → la casa (house)
  → la mesa (table)

⚠️ Common Exceptions:
• el día (day) - ends in -a but masculine
• la mano (hand) - ends in -o but feminine

💡 Helpful Endings:

Almost always feminine:
• -ción, -sión → la estación, la visión
• -dad, -tad → la ciudad, la libertad

Often masculine (Greek origin):
• -ma, -pa, -ta → el problema, el mapa, el planeta

sections.subtitle: Singular & Plural Forms
sections.content:
🔢 Plural Formation Rules

1️⃣ Ends in vowel → add -s:
• gato → gatos (cats)
• casa → casas (houses)
• estudiante → estudiantes (students)

2️⃣ Ends in consonant → add -es:
• flor → flores (flowers)
• papel → papeles (papers)
• profesor → profesores (teachers)

3️⃣ Ends in -z → change to -ces:
• lápiz → lápices (pencils)
• luz → luces (lights)
• vez → veces (times)

⚠️ Special case:
• Accented vowel + -s → NO change
  → el lunes → los lunes
  → el martes → los martes

sections.subtitle: Definite Articles (The)
sections.content:
📍 Definite Articles = "The"

• el → masculine singular
  → el perro (the dog)
• la → feminine singular
  → la mesa (the table)
• los → masculine plural
  → los libros (the books)
• las → feminine plural
  → las casas (the houses)

✅ Spanish uses "the" MORE than English:
• With general categories
  → Me gusta el café (I like coffee)
• With abstract concepts
  → La libertad es importante
    (Freedom is important)

sections.subtitle: Indefinite Articles (A/An/Some)
sections.content:
📝 Indefinite Articles = "A/An/Some"

Singular:
• un → masculine
  → un perro (a dog)
  → un libro (a book)
• una → feminine
  → una mesa (a table)
  → una casa (a house)

Plural (= "some"):
• unos → masculine
  → unos libros (some books)
• unas → feminine
  → unas casas (some houses)

sections.subtitle: Contractions: al & del
sections.content:
🔗 Two MANDATORY Contractions

1️⃣ a + el = al (to the)
• Voy al parque
  → I go to the park
• Voy al cine
  → I go to the cinema

2️⃣ de + el = del (of/from the)
• El libro del profesor
  → The teacher's book
• Vengo del trabajo
  → I come from work

⚠️ ONLY with "el"!
• a + la = a la (no contraction)
• de + los = de los (no contraction)
• de + las = de las (no contraction)

sections.subtitle: When to Omit Articles
sections.content:
🚫 When to OMIT Articles

1️⃣ Professions after "ser":
• Soy profesor (I am a teacher)
• Es médica (She is a doctor)

2️⃣ Languages (direct object):
• Hablo español (I speak Spanish)
• Estudio francés (I study French)

3️⃣ Days after "ser":
• Hoy es lunes (Today is Monday)
• Mañana es martes (Tomorrow is Tuesday)

4️⃣ Most cities/countries:
• Vivo en México (I live in Mexico)
⚠️ Exceptions: la Argentina, el Perú

5️⃣ With possessives:
• mi casa (my house)
  ❌ NOT la mi casa
• tu libro (your book)
  ❌ NOT el tu libro

questions.question: Which article is used with 'libro' (book)?
questions.hint: Words ending in -o are usually masculine. Use the masculine singular definite article.

questions.question: Which article is used with 'casa' (house)?
questions.hint: Words ending in -a are usually feminine. Use the feminine singular definite article.

questions.question: What is the plural of 'el gato' (the cat)?
questions.hint: Add -s to nouns ending in vowels. The article also changes to plural masculine.

questions.question: What is the plural of 'la flor' (the flower)?
questions.hint: Add -es to nouns ending in consonants. The article changes to plural feminine.

questions.question: What is the plural of 'el lápiz' (the pencil)?
questions.hint: Words ending in -z change to -ces in the plural. Remember to change the article too.

questions.question: Which noun is an EXCEPTION to the -o = masculine rule?
questions.hint: This body part ends in -o but is feminine. You say 'la mano', not 'el mano'.

questions.question: Which noun is an EXCEPTION to the -a = feminine rule?
questions.hint: This time word ends in -a but is masculine. You say 'el día', not 'la día'.

questions.question: What is the correct indefinite article for 'perro' (dog)?
questions.hint: Use the masculine singular indefinite article (a/an). Perro is masculine.

questions.question: What is the correct indefinite article for 'mesa' (table)?
questions.hint: Use the feminine singular indefinite article (a/an). Mesa is feminine.

questions.question: How do you say 'some books' in Spanish?
questions.hint: Use the masculine plural indefinite article. Libros is masculine plural.

questions.question: What does 'a + el' contract to?
questions.hint: This contraction means 'to the'. Example: Voy al parque (I go to the park).

questions.question: What does 'de + el' contract to?
questions.hint: This contraction means 'of the' or 'from the'. Example: el libro del profesor.

questions.question: Which is correct: 'I go to the park'?
questions.hint: Use the contraction 'al' (a + el) for 'to the' with masculine singular nouns.

questions.question: Does 'a + la' form a contraction?
questions.hint: Contractions only occur with 'el', not with 'la', 'los', or 'las'.

questions.question: Words ending in '-ción' are usually...
questions.hint: Think of 'la estación', 'la canción', 'la nación'. This ending is a strong indicator.

questions.question: Words ending in '-dad' are usually...
questions.hint: Think of 'la ciudad', 'la libertad', 'la universidad'. This ending pattern is reliable.

questions.question: In 'Soy profesor' (I am a teacher), why is there no article?

answers.text: It's a mistake, should be 'Soy un profesor'
Articles are always optional in Spanish

questions.hint: When stating professions with the verb 'ser', Spanish omits the indefinite article.

questions.question: How do you say 'I speak Spanish'?
questions.hint: Languages don't use articles when they're the direct object of a verb like 'hablar'.

questions.question: Which is correct for 'Today is Monday'?
questions.hint: When stating what day it is with 'ser', don't use an article before the day.

questions.question: Which is correct for 'my house'?
questions.hint: Don't use articles with possessive adjectives. It's either 'mi' or 'la', never both.
